subject: Concord Health — EastUS2 routing cutover & exec briefing
messages:
From: Concord Platform Ops <sre@concordhealth.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
Cc: Danielle Kaur <dkaur@concordhealth.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Realtime: EastUS2 — sustained latency/5xx spike (urgent)

Jasmine,

We started seeing a sustained 5xx and P95 latency jump across our EastUS2 footprint at ~07:45 PDT. Error rate peaked at ~12% and token throughput dropped ~40% for our production routing group (customer-facing traffic). Attached is a short heatmap (diag-heatmap.png) that shows the spike correlating with routing attempts to az-eastus2-a.

This is causing downstream customer pages to fail and our on-call is getting paged. Can Redwood initiate a cross-region diversion (start 10% -> EastUS1 then ramp) and open an ops bridge? We need exec attention and a short window for a controlled cutover.

Ping: Priya Shah (Concord), Danielle (platform).

Thanks,
Concord Platform Ops
SRE Team

Attachments: diag-heatmap.png
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.com>
To: Priya Shah <pshah@concordhealth.com>, Concord Platform Ops <sre@concordhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: EastUS2 — sustained latency/5xx spike (urgent)

Priya / SRE team — thanks for the alert and the heatmap.

Acking and taking point. I am opening an ops bridge now and looping the account + routing leads. We will follow our cross-region cutover checklist (attached) and initiate a staged diversion: 10% traffic to EastUS1 for 10 minutes, validate error rates, then 50% if stable.

Proposed immediate actions:
- Open bridge: CH-3124 (joining in 2m)
- Canary: 10% -> EastUS1 now, monitor P95 and 5xx rates
- Fallback: immediate rollback policy if 5xx increases beyond current baseline

I will post live updates in the bridge and ticket (link: https://redwood.app/ops/bridges/CH-3124). Please confirm you are OK with the staged diversion and that Concord will accept temporary connection changes.

-Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Account Lead, Strategic Customers

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Realtime: EastUS2 — sustained latency/5xx spike (urgent)

Technical plan (short):

1) Open bridge and set monitoring dashboards to 30s resolution.
2) Initiate 10% weight move to EastUS1 using routing policy: 
   - command: redwoodctl route adjust --policy concord-prod --from eastus2 --to eastus1 --weight 10
3) Observe P95 and 5xx for 10 minutes; if P95 drops >20% and 5xx < 3% absolute decrease, ramp to 50% for 5 minutes.
4) If 5xx rises or latency worsens, execute rollback immediately.

Fallback: if EastUS1 shows problems, fallback to internal fallback-model (quantized variant) in same region and notify Concord of possible longer-term pinning.

I have prepared a short canary script on the bridge and will watch traces. Asking Concord SRE to confirm readiness to accept the small routing change.

Priya / team — we are initiating the staged diversion now per plan above.

What we are doing now:
- Starting 10% weight to EastUS1 (canary)
- Monitoring P95 / 5xx on the bridge dashboard and application traces
- If stable at 10% for 10 minutes, will move to 50% for additional validation
- Rollback plan in place (0->100 rollback automation)

Please confirm: Concord SRE accepts this change and will report any observed failures on the bridge.

Live status will be posted to the ops bridge and I will send an exec note if we need to move to a full cutover.

Concord will hold procurement and credit requests until a post-mortem; please include logs and the final incident timeline. We have forwarded the thread internally and procurement will engage on any formal SLA credit (see concord-sla-req.pdf).

Appreciate the quick coordination. Please keep the exec bridge updated and we will standby for the post-mortem.

- Priya
